subproblem.title: A C¹ map injective on a closed ball with injective derivative maps the open ball onto an embedded C¹ submanifold
subproblem.statement: For all n, p ∈ ℕ (ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), every map G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ, every x ∈ ℝⁿ and every r ∈ ℝ, assume three things: G is of class C¹ on the closed ball B̄_r(x) = Metric.closedBall x r (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G (B̄_r(x))); G is injective on B̄_r(x); and the Fréchet derivative DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z is injective for every z in the open ball B_r(x) = Metric.ball x r. Then G(B_r(x)) is an n-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold of ℝᵖ in the sense of IsC1Submanifold n. That is, for every y ∈ G(B_r(x)) there are an open V ⊆ ℝⁿ, an open W ⊆ ℝᵖ with y ∈ W, and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ such that: ψ is C¹ and injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ G(B_r(x)); V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W; and fderiv ℝ ψ z is injective for every z ∈ V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn p) (x : Rn n) (r : ℝ), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G (Metric.closedBall x r) → Set.InjOn G (Metric.closedBall x r) → (∀ z ∈ Metric.ball x r, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G z)) → IsC1Submanifold n (G '' Metric.ball x r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 61-64 (printed p. 70): “G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold ... (with G_ij providing a local representation in a neighborhood of the point y = G_ij(x))”. The submanifold notion is Ch. 2 (4.1) (chapter-02.txt lines 849-860), transcribed as IsC1Submanifold. This lemma is the topological half of that remark: Steps 6-9 of the supplied proof of node root.submanifold_cover-a1.regular_ball_submanifold-a1. Two specializations apply. First, the closed ball B̄ there is B̄_r(x) itself. Erratum (v) of the parent asks for injectivity on a closed ball containing B̄_σ(x), and injectivity on B̄_σ(x) itself suffices, so the set A below is the sphere B̄_r(x) ∖ B_r(x). Second, G need only be C¹ on B̄_r(x).

Notation. ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). B_r(x) = Metric.ball x r and B̄_r(x) = Metric.closedBall x r. DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z.

Hypotheses. n, p ∈ ℕ; G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ; x ∈ ℝⁿ; r ∈ ℝ; G is C¹ on B̄_r(x) (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G (B̄_r(x))); G is injective on B̄_r(x); DG(z) is injective for every z ∈ B_r(x).
Goal. IsC1Submanifold n S, where S := G(B_r(x)).

1. Regularity. Since G is C¹ on B̄_r(x), it is continuous on B̄_r(x) (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Since B_r(x) ⊆ B̄_r(x) (Metric.ball_subset_closedBall), G is C¹ on B_r(x) (ContDiffOn.mono).

2. The chart data. Let V := B_r(x), A := B̄_r(x) ∖ B_r(x) and W := ℝᵖ ∖ G(A).
- V is open (Metric.isOpen_ball).
- ℝⁿ is a proper metric space, so B̄_r(x) is compact (isCompact_closedBall). A is a compact set minus an open set, hence compact (IsCompact.diff).
- A ⊆ B̄_r(x), so G is continuous on A (Step 1). Hence G(A) is compact (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn) and so closed in the Hausdorff space ℝᵖ (IsCompact.isClosed). Therefore W is open.

3. S ⊆ W, hence W ∩ S = S. Let z ∈ V and suppose G(z) ∈ G(A), say G(z) = G(a) with a ∈ A. Then a ∈ A ⊆ B̄_r(x) and z ∈ B_r(x) ⊆ B̄_r(x). Injectivity of G on B̄_r(x) gives a = z. So z = a ∉ B_r(x), contradicting z ∈ V. Hence G(z) ∈ W for every z ∈ V, i.e. S ⊆ W, and therefore W ∩ S = S.

4. Properness. Let K ⊆ W be compact. Claim: V ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K).
- ⊆: B_r(x) ⊆ B̄_r(x).
- ⊇: let z ∈ B̄_r(x) with G(z) ∈ K. If z ∉ B_r(x), then z ∈ A, so G(z) ∈ G(A) = ℝᵖ ∖ W. This contradicts G(z) ∈ K ⊆ W. Hence z ∈ B_r(x) = V.
K is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝᵖ, hence closed. G is continuous on the closed set B̄_r(x) (Metric.isClosed_closedBall). So B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) is closed (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed). It is a closed subset of the compact set B̄_r(x), hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). By the claim, V ∩ G⁻¹(K) is compact.

5. Verification of IsC1Submanifold n S. Let y ∈ S. Take V and W from Step 2 and ψ := G. Then:
- V is open and W is open (Step 2);
- y ∈ S ⊆ W (Step 3);
- ψ is C¹ on V (Step 1);
- ψ is injective on V, because V ⊆ B̄_r(x) and G is injective there (Set.InjOn.mono);
- ψ(V) = S = W ∩ S (Step 3);
- V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W (Step 4);
- fderiv ℝ ψ z = DG(z) is injective for every z ∈ V (hypothesis).
These are exactly the eight conditions of IsC1Submanifold n S at y.

6. Degenerate cases. If r ≤ 0, then B_r(x) = ∅ and S = ∅, so the statement holds vacuously; the argument above needs no change. The same argument covers n = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: G is continuous on B̄_r(x) and C¹ on B_r(x), by restricting ContDiffOn on the closed ball.
A := B̄_r(x) ∖ B_r(x) is compact (closed ball minus open ball in a proper space). So G(A) is compact and closed, and W := ℝᵖ ∖ G(A) is open.
Injectivity of G on B̄_r(x) gives G(B_r(x)) ⊆ W, hence W ∩ G(B_r(x)) = G(B_r(x)).
For compact K ⊆ W, B_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K), which is a closed subset of the compact B̄_r(x) and hence compact.
The single chart (V, W, ψ) = (B_r(x), W, G) verifies all eight IsC1Submanifold n conditions at every y ∈ G(B_r(x)); fderiv injectivity on V is the hypothesis.

audit.reason: The prose and exact standalone Lean proposition agree, including arbitrary real r. Restricted regularity suffices: the boundary image is compact, its complement W is open, and closed-ball injectivity puts the open-ball image inside W. The stated preimage equality proves properness using continuity only on the closed ball. All remaining chart conditions follow explicitly; r≤0 and n=0 are covered. The proof is complete and independent, and its bare name is unreserved. Applying the first child with U=univ supplies both injectivity hypotheses and proves the frozen parent with σ=r; a doubled radius is unnecessary.

subproblem.title: Quantitative local injectivity of a C¹ map near a point with injective derivative
subproblem.statement: For all n, p ∈ ℕ (ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), with Euclidean norm |·|), every map G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ, every open set U ⊆ ℝⁿ such that G is of class C¹ on U (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G U), and every x ∈ U at which the Fréchet derivative DG(x) = fderiv ℝ G x is injective, there are r > 0 with closed ball B̄_r(x) = Metric.closedBall x r ⊆ U and c > 0 such that (i) c|z − z'| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')| for all z, z' ∈ B̄_r(x), and (ii) c|v| ≤ |DG(z)v| for all z ∈ B̄_r(x) and all v ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn p) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G U → ∀ x ∈ U, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G x) → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ Metric.closedBall x r ⊆ U ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ (∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall x r, ∀ z' ∈ Metric.closedBall x r, c * ‖z - z'‖ ≤ ‖G z - G z'‖) ∧ ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall x r, ∀ v : Rn n, c * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ G z v‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 61-64 (printed p. 70): “if the Jacobian [of] G_ij is non-zero at a point x, then there is a σ > 0 such that G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold”. This lemma is the analytic half of that remark: Steps 1-5 of the supplied proof of node root.submanifold_cover-a1.regular_ball_submanifold-a1, localized to an open set U on which G is C¹ (that node applies it with U = ℝⁿ). No printed erratum is involved.

Notation. ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). |·| is the Euclidean norm and ‖·‖ the operator norm on L(ℝⁿ, ℝᵖ). B_ρ(x) = Metric.ball x ρ, B̄_ρ(x) = Metric.closedBall x ρ, DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z, and L := DG(x).

Hypotheses. n, p ∈ ℕ; G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ; U ⊆ ℝⁿ open; G is C¹ on U (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G U); x ∈ U; L = DG(x) is injective.
Goal. There are r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and c > 0 such that
(i) c|z − z'| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')| for all z, z' ∈ B̄_r(x), and
(ii) c|v| ≤ |DG(z)v| for all z ∈ B̄_r(x) and v ∈ ℝⁿ.

1. Regularity of G on U. G is C¹ on U and 1 ≠ 0, so G is differentiable within U at every point of U (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn). U is open, so it is a neighbourhood of each of its points (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence G is differentiable at every z ∈ U (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt) and has Fréchet derivative DG(z) there (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt). Moreover z ↦ DG(z) is continuous on U as a map into L(ℝⁿ, ℝᵖ) with the operator norm (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, using 1 ≤ 1).

2. Lower bound for L. L is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ. By LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz there is K > 0 with |v − w| ≤ K|Lv − Lw| for all v, w ∈ ℝⁿ. Taking w = 0 (L0 = 0) gives |v| ≤ K|Lv|. Put c₀ := 1/K > 0. Then
 (2.1) c₀|v| ≤ |Lv| for every v ∈ ℝⁿ.
For n = 0 the lemma still supplies K > 0, and (2.1) holds trivially since v = 0.

3. Choice of r and c.
- U is open and x ∈ U, so there is δ₁ > 0 with B_{δ₁}(x) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff).
- DG is continuous on U at x (Step 1). So there is δ₂ > 0 such that ‖DG(z) − L‖ < c₀/2 for all z ∈ U with |z − x| < δ₂ (Metric.continuousOn_iff together with dist_eq_norm).
Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0, r := δ/2 > 0 and c := c₀/2 > 0. Let z ∈ B̄_r(x). Then |z − x| ≤ δ/2 < δ ≤ δ₁, so z ∈ B_{δ₁}(x) ⊆ U; this proves B̄_r(x) ⊆ U. Also z ∈ U and |z − x| < δ ≤ δ₂, so
 (3.1) ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ c₀/2 for every z ∈ B̄_r(x).

4. Proof of (i). Let h(w) := G(w) − Lw.
- For w ∈ B̄_r(x) ⊆ U, Step 1 and the linearity of L show that h has Fréchet derivative DG(w) − L at w, hence also within the set B̄_r(x).
- By (3.1), ‖DG(w) − L‖ ≤ c₀/2 for all w ∈ B̄_r(x).
- B̄_r(x) is convex (convex_closedBall).
The mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le) therefore gives, for all z, z' ∈ B̄_r(x),
 |h(z) − h(z')| ≤ (c₀/2)|z − z'|.
Its variant norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le' with φ = L gives the same bound directly. Since L is linear, h(z) − h(z') = (G(z) − G(z')) − L(z − z'), so
 (4.1) |(G(z) − G(z')) − L(z − z')| ≤ (c₀/2)|z − z'|.
By the triangle inequality (norm_le_norm_add_norm_sub),
 |L(z − z')| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')| + |(G(z) − G(z')) − L(z − z')|.
Combining this with (2.1) for v = z − z' and with (4.1):
 c₀|z − z'| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')| + (c₀/2)|z − z'|.
Hence c|z − z'| = (c₀/2)|z − z'| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')|.

5. Proof of (ii). Let z ∈ B̄_r(x) and v ∈ ℝⁿ.
- By the operator-norm bound and (3.1): |(DG(z) − L)v| ≤ ‖DG(z) − L‖|v| ≤ (c₀/2)|v|, where (DG(z) − L)v = DG(z)v − Lv.
- By the triangle inequality: |Lv| ≤ |DG(z)v| + |DG(z)v − Lv|.
With (2.1): c₀|v| ≤ |Lv| ≤ |DG(z)v| + (c₀/2)|v|. Hence c|v| = (c₀/2)|v| ≤ |DG(z)v|.

6. Conclusion. r > 0 satisfies B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (Step 3), c > 0, (i) holds (Step 4) and (ii) holds (Step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: Since U is open and G is C¹ on U, G is differentiable at every point of U with derivative DG, and DG is continuous on U.
LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz applied to the injective L = DG(x) on finite-dimensional ℝⁿ gives c₀ = 1/K > 0 with c₀|v| ≤ |Lv|.
Take δ = min(δ₁, δ₂) with B_{δ₁}(x) ⊆ U and ‖DG(z) − L‖ < c₀/2 for z ∈ U ∩ B_{δ₂}(x), and set r := δ/2 and c := c₀/2. Then B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and ‖DG − L‖ ≤ c₀/2 on B̄_r(x).
The mean value inequality for w ↦ G(w) − Lw on the convex B̄_r(x) gives |G(z) − G(z') − L(z − z')| ≤ (c₀/2)|z − z'|. With the triangle inequality this yields c|z − z'| ≤ |G(z) − G(z')|.
The operator-norm perturbation |(DG(z) − L)v| ≤ (c₀/2)|v| and the triangle inequality give c|v| ≤ |DG(z)v| on B̄_r(x).
